policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'of the Benjamites'. The qere's two-word spelling la-ben yemini and the ketiv's single-word li-bnyamini are the same gentilic and yield the same English; the verse has no note mapped to this unit and nothing in the wording distinguishes the orthography. Both readings remain permitted and the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV renders the name 'Shitrai', whose consonants are shin-tet-resh-yod, the ketiv spelling shtry. The qere shrty would transliterate as 'Shirtai', with resh before tet. The English proper name therefore distinguishes the ketiv against the base qere.
